This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/view.json`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__FormView__buttons.reset.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FormViewSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/index.mdx`  _(via FormViewSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object formViewButtonsResetRemoved), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object formViewButtonsResetRemoved))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/view.json`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__FormView__buttons.reset.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1287b2fa30a48113e71b42271668156bf13ce264` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `b5abf5cc21da83fbf0cf72338526c9873c282384` — the merge of head `f101f23dde29e843f34ca63bd8df1ef2fcea567e` into base `1287b2fa30a48113e71b42271668156bf13ce264`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

```sh

git fetch origin b5abf5cc21da83fbf0cf72338526c9873c282384 && git checkout b5abf5cc21da83fbf0cf72338526c9873c282384
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1287b2fa30a48113e71b42271668156bf13ce264 f101f23dde29e843f34ca63bd8df1ef2fcea567e && git checkout -B drift-repro 1287b2fa30a48113e71b42271668156bf13ce264 && git merge --no-ff f101f23dde29e843f34ca63bd8df1ef2fcea567e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1287b2fa30a48113e71b42271668156bf13ce264
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1287b2fa30a48113e71b42271668156bf13ce264` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f101f23dde29e843f34ca63bd8df1ef2fcea567e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__FormView__buttons.reset.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-form-view-buttons-reset-retired.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts (the `hits`), widened to the narrowing floor: packages/spec/liveness/view.json, packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/form-view-buttons-reset-retirement.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.test.ts, packages/spec/vitest.repo-tests.json, ui/apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/recordFormNavigation.ts, ui/packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/formButtonsDefaults.test.tsx, ui/packages/types/src/__tests__/object-form-unmirrored-members-6152.test.ts, ui/packages/types/src/objectql.ts, ui/packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/conversions/walk.ts (`mapViewPayloads`), packages/spec/src/conversions/types.ts (`retiredAfter`), packages/spec/src/conversions/apply.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts and packages/spec/src/ui/react-blocks.ts (`showReset`), packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts `submitBehavior` (L4655–4735), packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts (the stored-row seam), ui/packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx (L2770–2795), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordFormPage.tsx (L405–425)

Inputs read: card #27153 body and all five comments (6464317022, 6464891999, 6465263085, the claim 6469111181, the dev report 6471072004); PR #27269 body, its 20-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge base `7858c1d1`; the check-runs on the head. Check-run state at the time of this record: every `Lint` job green (ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, docs & code guards, repo & tooling, CI/release/engine, the three scoped jobs, `Lint & Repo Gates`), `Spec property liveness` green, `Check Changeset` green, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green, `PR-body guards` green, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` green; `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger`, `Test Core (1–8/8)` and `Test UI (1–16/16)` still in progress; nothing has failed. No gate verdict below is mine; the pending ones stay the merge queue's.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, read in the tree at the head.

1. **`FormViewSchema.buttons.reset` is refused at parse** — `retiredKey(FORM_VIEW_BUTTONS_RESET_RETIRED)` inside the live `z.object({…}).strict()` block (`view.zod.ts` L4906–4910), the same shape as the 592 other `retiredKey()` sites in the file (e.g. `addRecord.mode` L1899, `filterableFields` L3009). Reach: `FormViewSchema`, `view.form`, `view.formViews.*`, a ViewItem form record's `config`, the flattened form overlay, and `defineStack` as `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422 — each pinned with the prescription's first sentence and the migrate sentence (`form-view-buttons-reset-retirement.test.ts`). Typed `never`, so `tsc` refuses the authoring site. **Right.**
2. **`buttons.submit` and `buttons.cancel` are unchanged**; an unknown button keeps the strict block's own `unrecognized_keys` and never reads "was removed" (the control test). **Right.**
3. **D2 conversion `form-view-buttons-reset-removed`** (`registry.ts`): strips `reset` from `buttons` through `mapViewPayloads` (`walk.ts` L588 — ViewItem record `config`, container `form` / `formViews.*`, flattened overlay, discriminated by the schema's own discriminators) plus the assembled `viewItems` channel, exactly as its sibling `formViewPresentationTypesRemoved` (order 78) does. `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '18.2.0'` — the package label is the stable `18.2.0`, so the stamp is the one `retired-after.census.test.ts` demands, and the prescription's "removed in 18.3.0" is the next release, the convention the `addRecord.*` tombstones already follow. Idempotent by `stripKeys`; an empty `buttons` block is left as `{}` (parses, draws the defaults). Fixture: 4 notices, one per site. Entered in `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` at `order: 79`, in variable-name order between `formLayoutInlineGridToVertical` and `formViewOptionDefaultRemoved`. **Right** on reach, and the stored-row seam (`database-loader.ts` L884) replays it with `includeRetired` pinned and `console.warn`s once per row, so a stored row is never refused and the strip is logged.
4. **D3 semantic entry `ui-form-view-buttons-reset-retired`** naming its D2 in `conversionIds`; STEP18 rationale fragment inserted in `id` order with `order: 113` (= the previous ceiling 112 + 1; the two 112s are the header's sanctioned in-flight tie). `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` row `ui/FormView:buttons.reset`. JOIN row in the removal-version pin reading `FormViewSchema.shape.buttons.unwrap()`. **Right** on registration. **Wrong on content** of the D3 `replacement` / `reason` — see ④.
5. **`@object-ui/types` `ObjectFormSchema.buttons` loses `reset`** in the TypeScript interface and the zod mirror (`looseObject`, so a stray `reset` still passes the ui mirror unread, which is that mirror's standing posture). Every ui reader of the block is typed through this: `ObjectForm.foldFormButtons` L127 reads `ObjectFormSchema['buttons']`; `ObjectView` L2785 forwards `schema.form?.buttons`, whose type is the ui `ObjectFormSchema`'s own `buttons` picked through `ObjectFormSlotKey`; `RecordFormPage` L418 forwards an `any`; `FormPage.readFormButton` and `resolveFormViewChrome` read `submit` / `cancel` only. No ui caller reads `.reset` after the change (walked `ui/packages` and `ui/apps`, tests included; the one fixture that authored it is moved in this PR). **Right** — no ui caller breaks; `Type Check UI` is CI's to confirm.
6. **`ObjectForm.foldFormButtons` no longer folds `buttons.reset.show` onto `showReset`** — the key's only reader, and `showReset` lands on `resetOnSubmit` (`ObjectForm.tsx` L1972: `schema.showReset || schema.submitBehavior?.kind === 'continue' || …`). Removing the reader of a refused key is **right**; its behavioural consequence is judged in ④.
7. **Liveness** `props/form/children/buttons` stays `live` for `submit` / `cancel`, note re-written to record the sub-key removal (sub-keys are not drillable). **Right**; `Spec property liveness` is green on the head.
8. **Generated references** (`view.mdx`, `protocol.mdx`) regenerate the `buttons` shape to `{ submit?, cancel? }` and add the `[REMOVED]` row for `reset`, in the shape the `addRecord.*` rows already have. Read, not reviewed: consistent with the schema.
9. **Flat `showReset` on the object-form block** (`component.zod.ts` L6958, `react-blocks.ts` L274), `drawerSide` / `drawerWidth`: untouched, as the claim says. **Right** to leave: #27247 and #27159 own them, and `react-blocks.md` would otherwise move (Tier H).

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/27153-form-view-buttons-reset-retired.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@object-ui/plugin-form` minor, `@object-ui/types` minor (both ui packages publish, `private: false`). Carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO line and the one-line fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered form-view-buttons-reset-removed, ui-form-view-buttons-reset-retired`), both ids resolving in the registries this diff adds. The level follows the kind: a tombstoned key is `narrowed` ⇒ at least `minor` on each package the diff moves. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` are green on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — matches what the diff publishes. Level: right. The changeset's prose has one must-fix sentence (④ M1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: the block's `showReset` ("Show the reset button") maps to `resetOnSubmit` — carried by #27247 (open, filed by seat 1, body read; it says "Land after #27153's PR"). Answered: not narrowed here, correctly.
- Dev flag "hotcrm was not measured from this session" — **escalated, not blocking**: the producer census is in-repo only (0 producers outside two fixtures, both moved). A sibling-repo source that authors `buttons.reset` meets the tombstone with its prescription and `os migrate meta --from 17`, and a stored row there is converted at read, so nothing breaks silently; but the seat should run the pin's `judge` walk (or `git grep -n 'reset' -- '*.form.ts' '*.view.ts'`) over `hotcrm` before its spec bump and note the count on the card. (should-fix S1)
- Dev flag "worktree install ran with `--ignore-scripts`" — benign: nothing measured depended on `better-sqlite3`'s build script, and CI installs normally.
- Dev flags "`pnpm lint` not run locally", "`check:skill-examples` not run" — answered by the head's check-runs: `Lint · ESLint` green; `skills/**` is byte-identical (the diff touches no skill file).
- Claim premise "Serial constraints cleared: #27155 landed" — holds: #27155 is closed, and the head is a merge of `main` at `7858c1d1`, past it.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: does it take a declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real?

**The retirement itself holds.** `main` declares `buttons.reset: FormButtonConfigSchema` described "Reset button". Read in the live tree: no button bar draws one (components `form.tsx`, console `FormPage`, `ModalForm`, `DrawerForm`, `WizardForm`, `MasterDetailForm`), `reset.label` has no reader anywhere under `ui/`, and the single reader of `reset.show` is the `ObjectForm` fold that lands on `resetOnSubmit`. A key declared "button" that never produced a button is ADR-0049's enforce-or-remove case, and seat 1 ruled retire. The PR makes the spec's refusal real at the schema (tombstone, every door, `tsc`) and removes the consumer fold in the same PR, which is the right side of the "never narrow at the consumer" line: the key is gone at the spec first, and the reader goes with it. `drawerSide` / `drawerWidth` and the block's `showReset` are left for their own cards; narrowing them here would have moved a Tier H surface under a `domain:spec` claim. The D2 reach is complete for every form payload spelling and the assembled channel; stored rows replay it with a once-per-row warning; built artifacts enter through `applyArtifactForwardConversions` under the `18.2.0` stamp; sources get `os migrate meta --from 17`.

**Where it breaks — M1 (must-fix): the migration text misstates the replacement, and the behaviour change is undisclosed.** Today a stored or authored form view with `buttons: { reset: { show: true } }`, rendered through `ObjectView` (L2785) or `RecordFormPage` (L418) — the two entry points that forward `buttons` into `ObjectForm` — clears the form after every successful save (`foldFormButtons` L136 → `showReset` → `resetOnSubmit` L1972). After this PR the stored row is converted at read, the fold is gone, and that form stops clearing after save. The spec already has the declared spelling of exactly that effect: `submitBehavior: { kind: 'continue' }` — "reset the form so another response can be entered" (`view.zod.ts` L4666), "it just resets the form" (L4722), honoured by `ObjectForm` (`resetOnSubmit` L1973) and by console `FormPage` (L2458, back to the record as loaded). Yet the three strings that ship as the migration doc all say there is none:

- the tombstone prescription `FORM_VIEW_BUTTONS_RESET_RETIRED` (`view.zod.ts` L4555): "Delete the key: a form has `submit` and `cancel` buttons only, and Cancel leaves the form without saving." — `retiredKey()`'s own governing text (`retired-key.ts`): "State what replaced the key, the version that removed it, and the one-line fix — this string IS the migration doc for anyone who hits it";
- the D3 `replacement` (`18.ui-form-view-buttons-reset-retired.ts`): "nothing to write instead … Delete the key", and its `reason` names the wrong undecidable ("a way back to its opening values" vs Cancel) while the real one — whether a `show: true` author wanted clear-after-save — goes unnamed;
- the changeset FROM → TO: "There is nothing to write instead: Cancel leaves the form without saving."

These are the texts an upgrading agent greps (`CHANGELOG.md`, the upgrade guide, every refusal, every JSON Schema `describe`), and AGENTS.md says a factual error in a released entry is reachable only by a dedicated PR the reader never lands on. The behaviour change itself is stated nowhere in the present tense: the changeset and D3 describe what `show: true` *did*, never that a converted row *stops* doing it. Required, all prose, no shape change: (a) the prescription adds one sentence after "Delete the key", e.g. "A form that relied on `show: true` clearing the form after a save declares that with `submitBehavior: { kind: 'continue' }`."; (b) the D3 `replacement` names `submitBehavior: { kind: 'continue' }` for that case and `reason` names the undecidable as whether the author wanted the clear-after-save or a button; (c) the changeset's FROM → TO line says the same and states that a converted row no longer clears after save on `ObjectView` / `RecordFormPage`; (d) the conversion docblock likewise. Regenerate the references. The pins survive it: the new test matches `startsWith(FIRST_SENTENCE)` and `toContain(MIGRATE_SENTENCE)`, `view.test.ts` matches `/buttons\.reset.*was removed.*Delete the key/s`. ⛔ Do **not** fold the choice into D2 (`show: true` → `submitBehavior: continue`): `FormPage` never honoured `reset.show` but does honour `continue`, so a D2 mapping would add behaviour on an entry point that never had it — a semantic choice, which is what D3 exists to hand to the upgrading agent. The strip plus notice is the right D2.

**S1 (should-fix):** the hotcrm census, as in ③.

**S2 (should-fix):** `ObjectForm.tsx` L279 at the head still reads "FormViewSchema carries the structured `buttons.{submit,cancel,reset}.`" — a comment the PR's own edit to this file leaves behind, in the file that is this narrowing's consumer; the tree-scoped absence walk does not cover `ui/`, so nothing will catch it later.

Tried and holding: a `buttons` block that held only `reset` converts to `{}` and parses; a form without `reset` rides through by reference (no spurious notice, no re-save churn); the flattened-overlay arm is reached only with `config` absent, so a malformed `config` is left for the parse; the `viewItems` arm skips `viewKind !== 'form'`; the ui zod mirror's `looseObject` does not become a second door; the type-level removal from `@object-ui/types` has no remaining reader of `.reset`; `retiredAfter` equals the stable label so the artifact door opens for every artifact built on ≤ 18.2.0 and refuses nothing built after; the STEP18 insertion sits in `id` order with `order` = ceiling + 1.
